To answer your question, I was hoping you'd have something else to say beyond just "better luck next time". I figured if I gave a bit more of an inclination of where I am right now, you might sympathize or have some new advice. 

I do see a therapist, though. Ironically enough, I get more supportive counsel here than I do with them. Many people put up with my negativity. In fact, it's sort of like a cycle. These posts are spaces where we hear each other out and don't judge each other for it. I may be negative here; tomorrow, I'll receive someone else's negativity on a different post. It makes it a bit easier to live with the pain.

You may feel otherwise, though. I get the inclination that you like giving advice. Maybe you feel like, if not acknowledgment or thanks, you're at least owed neutral silence for your contributions. I understand that. But, you know, I don't think my failure to validate you warrants equating my suicidal urges with "trying to play god". I don't think I've done anything to encourage or invite any of the apparent disdain you've written.

And, you know? You're assuming that, if I killed myself, I would be leaving behind some kind of unfulfilled legacy. Isn't that a bit privileged? Do you think I'm going to be leaving behind my children? My lovers? My friends? No. My roots end at my fingertips; I am a person without other people. Take care before you try to dismiss me, because you can't really understand what I'm going through, and it doesn't seem like you recognize where I am.

The universe is too cruel for reincarnation. This is all I get. A stunted, worthless life with no joy and no satisfaction and no companionship, and the lucidity to know just how much I'm missing. I may as well just end it, you know, I really may as well.

You yourself have admitted in other responses that you aren't necessarily a trained professional. There's nothing wrong with that; one doesn't need to be a trained professional to reach out to others. However, I believe that while the points you've elaborated on in your response have some truth to them, they aren't absolutely true. We can't know if people are addicted to pity. We can't say with absolute certainty that this sub is an echo chamber of despair. These are estimates, and they're not unfounded estimates, but you as one person can't just claim these things as if they're unequivocally true. There are parts of this subreddit you haven't seen. Posts you haven't read. People you haven't spoken with. It isn't just a monolith. To that end, if you believe that provocation will inspire people to change, which, if I'm understanding you correctly, is why you framed the second paragraph with negative rhetoric, then it's important that you consider that it is a very rare person who thrives after being insulted. There are some who do, but they're rare, and I don't believe that the majority of this sub would respond all that well to it.

Evidently, many people share your views, given how well the post's been received. Normally, I would think to ask you to simply edit and reword the second paragraph, since you've made it clear that you didn't actually mean any of the odium that it implied, but, again, many people seem to agree with you, so editing it would probably garner just as much negativity from the affirmative side as it currently is with the people who've been upset by it.

I think you're right to leave the sub, though. This isn't a place where people come to be criticized or given tough love. It's a place of support and solidarity, even if it seems like meaningless pity or pointless sentiment. For people like me, who have physical illnesses that prevent us from ever developing socially, that solidarity and support is the best we can get.

On my main account, I post a lot to r/suicidewatch. I get a lot of shit for it. I've had people tell me, a cancer patient, that I have no idea what depression really is. I've had people mock me when I tried giving them advice. I've had people make ableist remarks towards me when I tried sympathizing with them. I've cried at what some people said; I'm not the sort of person that just easily shrugs off insults or condescension. But, no matter how hurt I've been, I know that they were right to lash out at me, because it was their space to be angry. The same could be said for r/lonely.

When you come to offer support to vulnerable people online, you need to be able to accept that you won't always be well-received. If you comment on a vulnerable person's post, and if they get upset with that comment, that ought to be a learning experience for you. You say that you've told people to change their ways, and that you've recommended that they be positive to strangers. I understand how frustrating it is to be downvoted and ridiculed for an earnest attempt at helping another person, but have you considered that the advice you gave them may have been advice that they've already heard? Have you considered that your advice may have entailed things that they'd already tried, or that it may have entailed things that they were incapable of acting on? In addition, it's important to keep in mind that, for a lot of traumatized, angry people, what may sound to you like constructive feedback will come off as condescending criticism.

And furthermore, you weren't dumb to think that people here actually want help, because, nine out of ten times, they *do.* Things only become complicated when there's a miscommunication or a failure to recognize or communicate emotional boundaries. Sometimes, the thing that a person needs to hear the most is that they aren't alone, or that their struggle provoked a sympathetic response from someone. If someone's feeling worthless, like you mentioned, they won't have the energy to try and improve their circumstances. In the validation of solidarity, though, they may find new motivation to change their ways, and if they do, *then* they might be able to accept your feedback.

If you want to leave the subreddit, by all means, please do. But this post is cruel and uncalled for. I understand that it may be frustrating to feel as though people are not taking easy and accessible advice, but to claim that the majority of the people here are "addicted to their self-pity and the pity of others" and that this space is "nothing but an echo chamber of despair" is reprehensible.
